title: Use uploaded app icon as browser tab favicon

requirements.summary: Add the uploaded favicon image (and resized variants) to publicly served frontend static assets.
acceptanceCriteria: `prompt-library-favicon.png` (or a derived favicon file created from it) is present in the frontend’s publicly served static assets so it can be loaded by the browser without backend involvement.

file_operations.description: Add the uploaded `prompt-library-favicon.png` into the publicly served static assets (copy from the provided asset into the frontend public assets directory).
Create a resized favicon asset derived from `prompt-library-favicon.png` at 32x32 pixels: `frontend/public/assets/generated/favicon.dim_32x32.png`.
Optionally create a resized favicon asset derived from `prompt-library-favicon.png` at 16x16 pixels for broader browser support: `frontend/public/assets/generated/favicon.dim_16x16.png`.

requirements.summary: Remove the embedded base64 favicon mechanism so it no longer determines the browser tab icon.
acceptanceCriteria: When loading the app in a browser, the tab displays the new favicon based on `prompt-library-favicon.png`.
Any existing favicon mechanism (including the embedded base64 favicon in `frontend/src/lib/favicon.ts`) no longer determines the tab icon.

file_operations.description: Remove the embedded base64 favicon data and update the utility so it does not set a base64 favicon (either deprecate the function or have it reference the new static favicon asset), ensuring this file no longer determines the tab icon.

requirements.summary: Set the favicon via a proper link tag in frontend/index.html without any UI/branding changes.
acceptanceCriteria: `frontend/index.html` includes a favicon link tag (or equivalent initialization occurs before the app renders) that points to the new favicon asset.
No visible UI components, headers, logos, or in-app icons are changed as part of this request.

file_operations.description: Add/replace favicon `<link rel="icon" ...>` tags in the HTML head to reference the new publicly served assets (use `frontend/public/assets/generated/favicon.dim_32x32.png` as the primary icon and `frontend/public/assets/generated/favicon.dim_16x16.png` as an additional size), ensuring it applies on initial page load and replaces any prior favicon behavior.
